newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago credit card chargeoff rate rises.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago credit card chargeoff rate rises.

text.p: First Chicago NBD Corp said Wednesday its credit card chargeoff rate rose to 6.7 percent of managed receivables in the fourth quarter, compared to 5.9 percent in the third quarter.

The $104.6 billion asset bank holding company also said it posted a trading profit of $12 million in the quarter, compared to a profit of $48 million a year ago and a loss of $12 million in the third quarter.
Total market-driven revenues rose to $83 million in the fourth quarter from $40 million in the third quarter, First Chicago said.

While the bank's credit card charge off rate rose, credit card fee revenue was $259 million, up 28 percent from a year ago, adjusting for securitization. Return on equity for the credit card business was more than 30 percent, the bank said.

First Chicago also said it repurchased 7.3 million shares of its common stock during the fourth quarter at an average price of $53.93 a share, adding that it has authorization to repurchase an additional 32.7 million shares under a program announced in October.
Earlier Wednesday, First Chicago said operating earnings were $377 million, or $1.14 a share in the fourth quarter, up from $318 million, or $0.96 a share a year ago.
First Chicago shares were down 1/2 at 53-5/8 in early trading Wednesday.
